claims.text: Peds: children w microalbuminuria on repeat samples or persistently ↑BP (> 90th–95th percentile for age, or ≥ 130/80 mm Hg in adolescents) despite lifestyle chgs typically need an antiHTN, most often an ACEi or ARB;
claims.quote: Children with microalbuminuria (albumin:creatinine ratio 30 to 300 mg/g) on repeat samples or with persistently elevated blood pressure readings (> 90th to 95th percentiles for age or ≥ 130/80 mm Hg for adolescents) who do not respond to lifestyle interventions typically require antihypertensive therapy, most commonly using an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor or angiotensin II receptor blocker

claims.text: counsel pts of childbearing potential about ACEis, ARBs and statins.
claims.quote: Appropriate counseling regarding angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors, angiotensin II receptor blockers, and statins should be provided to patients of childbearing potential.

claims.text: Indicated in diabetes w CKD (↓GFR or albuminuria) even w.o HTN;
claims.quote: ACE inhibitors or ARBs are indicated for patients with diabetes and evidence of chronic kidney disease (CKD) (decreased glomerular filtration rate or albuminuria), even in the absence of hypertension

claims.text: first-line for diabetes + HTN regardless of CKD.
claims.quote: They are the first-line treatment for patients with diabetes and hypertension regardless of CKD status.
